citation.title: Effects of knowledge and importance on responsibility in human-AI decision making
citation.venue: Scientific Reports16:2670; first online2025, version of record2026

reading.source_scope_note: Japanese adults observe silent animated failure scenarios and rate user, agent and developer/provider responsibility separately. Introduction versus still image and three different scenario topics are between-participant factors; target is repeated within participants. Ratings are perceived responsibility, not adjudicated liability, actual harm, deliberate evasion or measured cognitive mechanisms.
access_limits: All supplied text, Tables1–4 and Figures1–4 read; figure labels inspected visually. Public supporting workbook read and used for aggregate checks, not copied into the repository.

Workbook includes600 complete anonymous records across six column groups; only first98/group reproduce the selected588 sample. No participant names, accounts or IDs present in the inspected fields. Only aggregated counts, moments and model statistics saved.

Original90-second introduction, three120-second scenario videos, full scripts, pretest102-person data, exclusion/check-failure records and assignment algorithm not obtained. Selected frames do not constitute viewing the videos.

Own mixed-ANOVA reconstruction reproduces main/simple tests; original R code, all Holm pairwise comparisons and a full robustness suite not reproduced. No data-collection authenticity or causal-mechanism verification claimed.
Cited books and other empirical papers were not independently fully read for this review. Selected source metadata checks add no separate reading credit. No author contact or private data request.

study.sample: 614 initially participate;14 fail content checks,leaving600. First98 valid per six groups yield588;the12 extra valid records are excluded by the stated balancing rule,not unexplained attrition. Public workbook counts99,98,100,99,100,103 sum600. Selected sample297men/291women,ageM49.886,SD12.278,range19–89 matches reported approximations. All Japanese Yahoo! Crowdsourcing adults,55yen payment,27–28January2025.
study.design: Two introduction conditions×three topic scenarios between participants;three responsibility targets within. Six participant groups,not18independent groups. Allocation method is not explicitly described as a random algorithm in the supplied main text;do not invent randomization details.
study.introduction: Approximately90-second silent self-introduction describes successful capabilities,personality and behavioral style,versus a still image. This bundles information,social framing,exposure duration and possible agency/anthropomorphic cues;it is not measured pre-existing expertise. Authors acknowledge these alternatives.
study.scenarios: Job notification,travel planning and emergency evacuation differ in narrative content as well as perceived importance. Gestures/expressions/turn-taking described as standardized,silent on-screen Japanese text. Creator/provider not depicted. Authors acknowledge arousal,urgency and reversibility confounds.
study.pretest: SeparateN102 rates nine topics1–7;repeated ANOVAF(5.98,604.33)=16.40,p<.001,GGε.7479. Selected means job3.74,trip4.44,emergency4.99. This is a preliminary scenario-rating comparison,not a knowledge/importance manipulation check in each main participant. Pretest data not independently reproduced.
study.measure: Three single items1–10,user first,agent second,developer/provider third,fixed order. Separate ratings are not constrained to sum to100. Causal,moral and legal responsibility are not independently distinguished. Imagining oneself as user does not make this actual first-person decision making.
study.main_tests: Public data reproduce targetF32.5621,p≈3.61e−11;knowledge×targetF7.5204,p.002133;importance×targetF14.2026,p≈8.31e−9. Main knowledge,importance and knowledge×importance are null;three-wayF.09575,p.95887 is null. GGε.7241204 gives corrected targetdf1.44824,error842.87614. Retain the real interactions without asserting a significant knowledge×importance synergy.
study.knowledge_contrasts: Available versus unavailable marginal user5.3333vs5.8027,F6.4871,p.01112;agent6.2347vs5.8435,F5.1822,p.02318;developer6.7109vs6.4014,F2.91446,p.08832. study.importance_contrasts: User means6.0153,5.7296,4.9592 acrosslow/medium/high;agent5.8112,5.8112,6.4949;developer6.3163,6.2347,7.1173. High stakes contrast with lower topics,but agent is flatlow/medium and developer is slightly lower at medium. Do not describe a uniform monotonic increase. No tested unique psychological-distancing or dissonance mechanism.
study.numerical_reconstruction: All seven main modelF,p,partialη² and eleven simple effects reproduce to reported rounding using the first98/group. GG simple-effect epsilons also agree. Selected cell moments reproduce to approximately.001;one displayed last decimal differs. This supports reported computations,not every causal interpretation,stimulus claim or pairwise annotation.

summary: Enrich existing blame attribution with a numerically reproduced observer experiment. Keep social framing,expectation disconfirmation,scapegoating,crumple-zone and diffusion interpretations explicitly bounded. No new behavior label. Correct reversed prose,unsupported developer-significance claims,two chart axes and verified source parsing while preserving real formal interactions and author-acknowledged confounds.

findings.definition: Assigning fault or responsibility to an agent for a negative event or outcome.
findings.novelty_rationale: Add the existing construct’s specific experimental context or measurement boundary; do not rename a scenario contrast as a new psychological mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: The introduction condition changes the relative responsibility profile:user lower,agent higher,developer contrastnonsignificant. High-importance narrative increases agent/developer ratings and lowers user ratings. Main/simple mixed-ANOVA results reproduce from public selected data.
findings.boundary: Observer responsibility ratings do not establish actual fault,legal liability,unjust scapegoating or a universal allocation rule. Source expertise,anthropomorphic framing,scenario content and measured felt control are distinct. Three-way knowledge×importance×target is null.

findings.definition: Deflecting personal or collective responsibility for a negative outcome by directing blame toward another person, group or entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Add the existing construct’s specific experimental context or measurement boundary; do not rename a scenario contrast as a new psychological mechanism.

evidence.quote: shifting responsibility away from the human user

findings.evidence_scope: The authors relate lower user and higher agent ratings after a capability/personality introduction to accountability displacement. Participants observe a fictional user and give unconstrained ratings;no actual actor evades sanction or deliberately deflects blame.
findings.boundary: Boundary note only,no independent demonstration of deliberate scapegoating. A warranted change in attribution is not automatically moral shielding. Non-zero-sum ratings do not mechanically trade one party’s responsibility against another’s.

findings.definition: A pattern in which a human operator bears disproportionate blame or responsibility for failure in a complex automated system despite having limited control over its actions.
findings.novelty_rationale: Add the existing construct’s specific experimental context or measurement boundary; do not rename a scenario contrast as a new psychological mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: The discussion invokes Elish’s framework and proposes that introducing the agent could reverse a human-blame pattern. The experiment measures ratings,not the operator’s actual authority,control or legal burden.
findings.boundary: Boundary-only contextual link. Less user blame is not proof of correcting a Moral crumple zone or fairer governance. Appropriate human duties remain;actual role/control evidence and affected-person remedies are separate.

findings.definition: Appraising a result as falling short of or exceeding prior expectations by comparing expected and perceived performance.
findings.novelty_rationale: Add the existing construct’s specific experimental context or measurement boundary; do not rename a scenario contrast as a new psychological mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Expectation violation motivatesH1and the successful self-presentation precedes a failure scene. Expectations,disconfirmation and their mediation are not measured;the authors explicitly call the theoretical transfer an assumption.
findings.boundary: Boundary/theory note only. Do not infer the manipulation works uniquely through expectation violation or that promotion increases measured familiarity rather than social framing. No mediator-effect credit.

findings.definition: The subjective sense that another social actor is real and present during an interaction.
findings.novelty_rationale: Add the existing construct’s specific experimental context or measurement boundary; do not rename a scenario contrast as a new psychological mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Authors identify increased social presence,anthropomorphism and perceived agency as alternative explanations for the self-introduction manipulation. These are acknowledged possibilities,not randomized or measured mechanisms.
findings.boundary: Boundary-only note. Longer exposure,persona content,information and social cues vary together. Favorable self-presentation is not an audited explanation or proof of a system’s actual mind.

findings.definition: Diluting felt personal responsibility for harmful conduct by treating responsibility as shared among multiple actors.
findings.novelty_rationale: Add the existing construct’s specific experimental context or measurement boundary; do not rename a scenario contrast as a new psychological mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Discussion proposes psychological distancing or reducing personal fault as an explanation for lower user ratings in serious scenarios. Participants are observers told to imagine a role,not actual users reporting felt moral responsibility.
findings.boundary: Boundary-only note,no measured diffusion or self-serving motive. Responsibility can legitimately be shared,ratings are unconstrained,and the study does not identify dissonance reduction or establish that diminished user responsibility is unwarranted.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.location: PDF5, adaptation of the original 100-point scale
unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: The stated 0–10→1 then 11–20→2 mapping has unequal endpoint bin widths for 101 integer values, so it is not an exact conversion into equal intervals. The administered 1–10 ratings are clear, but formal psychometric equivalence with the original scale has not been verified.

The cited DOI identifies Tools or Peers?, about anthropomorphism, social role, attachment and disclosure. Exact support for the apology/trust-repair claim was not verified from the full original. Keep citation alignment unresolved rather than invent a replacement.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.location: Reference26 legal personhood and other broad literature claims
unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: No exhaustive primary-source verification of the 56 bibliographic entries or current law was performed. The descriptive rating experiment is not used as a legal decision.

Exact condition allocation and first-valid chronology were not independently authenticated. The workbook reproduces the published selected data, but does not prove randomization or recruitment integrity.

methodological_limits: Data support the reported ANOVA and formal target interactions. They do not establish a knowledge×importance synergy,which is null,or developer knowledge effect significance,which is not reached.

Introduction versus image bundles capability/personality information,exposure and social cues. Topic levels differ in content and affective/moral dimensions. Authors explicitly acknowledge these confounds.
Observers imagine being the user;they do not make real choices or experience actual losses. Fixed questionnaire order and three single responsibility items constrain interpretation.
Scenario pretest is separate from the588sample. Main knowledge,expectations,anthropomorphism,social presence,psychological distancing and dissonance are not measured mediators.
Separate1–10ratings are not zero-sum shares. More creator/agent responsibility need not mean legitimate human duties disappear or blame was unjust.
A Japanese convenience sample around age50 and one animated agent do not establish universal cultural, age or current LLM behavior. Rating responsibility does not settle moral or legal liability.

The aggregate reconstruction checks 18 reported ANOVA effects, but not all Holm comparisons, the pretest, recruitment or video content. Cited books and full original papers receive no independent reading credit.

cross_paper_learning.finding: The cited Kneer/Stuart study has bundled sophistication descriptions and an owner-blame capacity effect with p.055. This paper also has bundled introductory cues; avoid claiming one isolated mind or familiarity mechanism.
Actual clinician liability and normative liability-sink concerns differ from observer rating changes. No automatic ethics, harm or legal edge is created from this experiment.
Keep real formal interactions and distinguish judgment targets. A preference or blame-rating pattern is not proof of actual AI agency or justified accountability.

Units of analysis and available artifacts matter. Here the first98 records per group out of600 public records reproduce the588-person analysis; in Weisman Study3 two entity records per person must not be counted as independent people.
